An approach based on elasticity-plasticity and cyclic stress-strain curves for a specific RPV material is more appropriate.

A source of inaccuracies is the application of simplified Ke-factors, especially those given by the ASME approach. They often result in strong over-conservatism, but also nonconservative results are possible. In some cases, ratcheting can also be a topic of interest, which also requires realistic cyclic stress-strain curves.

Concerning piping, auxiliary lines may be affected by fatigue. In that case, this results from thermohydraulic loading related to dead legs behaviour as the main uncertainty for these components is the loading.

*Importance for LTO beyond 60 years:* The fatigue life of all fatigue-sensitive loaded structural components should be assured for all significantly fatigue loaded areas without exception based on state-of-the-art methodology.

*Proposal for dispositioning:* Implementation of an experimental programme for the determination of cyclic stress-strain curves for specific RPV materials and performance of required fatigue analysis.

Introducing these cyclic stress-strain curves into the design codes. For numerical ratcheting analyses, clear requirements are needed for the constitutive model and guidance for setting the model parameters. Only models that include nonlinear kinematic hardening are appropriate to handle ratcheting (in the most common FE-codes ANSYS and ABAQUS, only the Chaboche-model fulfils this requirement).

*Relevant sub-section of the report:* 4.3. Reactor pressure vessel internals

*Conclusion number:* E4.3-01

*Conclusion title:* IASCC behaviour in LWR environments: data and models for LTO beyond 60 years

*Description of conclusion:* There is a need to continue carrying out experimental tests and modelling developments to improve the prediction of SCC and IASCC affecting internals. This covers analytical and service conditions testing, OPEX analysis as well as the development of advanced physically based modelling.

The current model for IASCC crack growth rates (ASME Code Case N-889) in PWR environment (low potential environment) is limited to 20 dpa by an NRC condition in the United States. The NRC imposed the condition due to some crack growth rates above 20 dpa not being bounded by the code case model, and the scarcity of data at doses > 20 dpa. Significant portions of the baffle plate assembly exceeded this dose after 40 years of operation and the volume of material above 20 dpa will increase with time. To disposition flaws in regions of the baffle plate assembly exceeding 20 dpa, it will be necessary to expand the dose range of the IASCC crack growth rate model.

A separate problem is IASCC for VVER materials, namely Ti-stabilised austenitic stainless steel 08CH18N10T, since its evaluation IASCC is based on experimental data obtained for other type steels. It is necessary to establish reliable ISI methods to determine any possible IASCC crack specifically in baffle-former bolts. These may have different designs for different VVERs and consequently different requirements for NDE inspection methods.

The IASCC behaviour in LWR environments for the full range of dose relevant for operation beyond 60 years, as well as long-term aspects related to SCC susceptibility, are issues that need to be addressed. The presence of numerous tiny He bubbles in highly irradiated SSs noted above, as well as void swelling, could affect FT and IASCC susceptibility and therefore need better understanding.

*Importance for LTO beyond 60 years:* SCC and IASCC affect several internal components. The damage is under control today due to the maintenance carried out. Nevertheless, in the long term, improving SCC and IASCC prediction remains an important objective to prevent or anticipate the appearance of unexpected degradations and to secure dedicated maintenance operations.

IASCC behaviour of highly irradiated Ti-stabilised austenitic stainless steels (used in VVERs) can differ from highly irradiated Co-stabilised austenitic stainless steels (used in PWRs), so it needs to be studied separately.

Since the susceptibility to IASCC increases with fluence, the probability for failures caused by this phenomenon can be anticipated to increase with longer operational time.

*Proposals for dispositioning:* Perform IASCC testing (initiation and propagation) and microstructural characterisation of materials at high fluence levels using components harvested from decommissioned PWRs. Improve understanding of the role of He on the IASCC susceptibility and generate quantitative data for the extension of existing models and predictive tools for IASCC. Implement the VVER specific research programme investigating the corrosion behaviour of irradiated Ti-stabilised austenitic stainless steel.

*Relevant sub-section of the report:* 4.3. Reactor pressure vessel internals

*Conclusion number:* E4.3-02

*Conclusion title:* Irradiation embrittlement of SS and SS welds of RPVIs

*Description of conclusion:* Irradiation embrittlement of internal materials exposed to high energy neutrons results in a loss of toughness. This data could be useful if a crack is observed or postulated on a component subjected to significant irradiation such as RPVIs. If the local applied stress intensity at the crack tip exceeds the reduced FT, crack evolution is considered as unstable.

Irradiation embrittlement and the effect of high neutron fluence on the FT of austenitic materials, in particular SS welds (e.g. in core barrels and core shrouds), are identified as a low-knowledge, high-susceptibility research item in NUREG/CR-7153 Vol 2 [43]. Additional data that expand the current database in terms of dose and with more heats/welds, as well as improved mechanistic understanding regarding the factors controlling embrittlement, are needed to improve the capability to predict the embrittlement of SS and SS welds beyond 60 years of operation.

*Importance for LTO beyond 60 years:* Structural integrity verification of RPVIs can be challenging without data and models covering the full range of dose at the end of intended LTO, for e.g. 80 years of operation or more. This information should be used to develop or improve models predicting irradiation embrittlement in RPVIs beyond 60 years of operation.

*Proposals for dispositioning:* Perform FT testing, including detailed fractographic examination, and microstructural characterisation of irradiated wrought SS and SS welds harvested from decommissioned BWRs and PWRs. Specimens fabricated from components harvested from decommissioned LWRs can potentially be further irradiated in a materials test reactor with a neutron spectrum representative of LWRs to doses corresponding to for example 80 years of operation. Following further irradiation, FT testing, microstructural characterisation, and development of a predictive model should be carried out.

*Relevant sub-section of the report:* 4.3 Reactor pressure vessel internals

*Conclusion number:* E4.3-03

*Conclusion title:* Wear affecting internals: data and models for LTO beyond 60 years

*Description of conclusion:* Carrying out experimental tests and modeling developments to improve the prediction of wear affecting internals. This covers analytical and service conditions testing, OPEX analysis as well as the development of advanced physically based modeling. This also covers the development of models for the simulation of flows in the RPV and the induced vibrations of RVI.

*Importance for LTO beyond 60 years:* Wear affects several internal components such as lower and upper guide parts, upper guide tubes as well as the thermal sleeves and cluster guides. The damage is under control today due to the maintenance carried out. Nevertheless, in the long term, improving wear prediction remains an important objective to have adequate maintenance.

*Proposals for dispositioning:* Studies to better quantify wear prediction affecting internals.

*Relevant sub-section of the report:* 4.3 Reactor pressure vessel internals

*Conclusion number:* E4.3-04

*Conclusion title:* Repair of highly irradiated materials of RPVIs

*Description of conclusion:* The development of repair methods applicable to highly irradiated materials of RPVIs covers research on welding of irradiated materials considering advanced welding processes. Helium accumulation in irradiated SSs makes welding of such components challenging. R&D is still to be done to qualify adapted repair methods. Other methods than welding should also be investigated.

*Importance for LTO beyond 6 years:* The development of methods for repairing irradiated RPVIs provides an alternative to replacement in cases where this operation would be complex to carry out. In the perspective of continued operation of reactors beyond 60 years, this is therefore an important objective. No industrial deadline is required currently.

*Proposals for dispositioning:* Development of methods for repairing irradiated internal components.

*Relevant sub-section of the report:* 4.3. Reactor pressure vessel internals

*Conclusion number:* E4.3-05

*Conclusion title:* Environmental effects on fatigue resistance of neutron irradiated materials

*Description of conclusion:* The knowledge regarding the effects of irradiation on environmental fatigue resistance is very limited. Longer operational times of LWRs introduce additional load transients associated with startup and shutdown and an increased probability for unplanned load transients. In addition, the fluence of the RPVIs increases with time. The synergetic combination of these factors is unknown and should be assessed to secure the justification of long-term operation of RPVIs against EAF.

A separate problem is the fatigue curves for VVER RPVI components since the fatigue behaviour of VVER RPVI materials in a VVER primary water environment may differ from the fatigue behaviour of austenitic stainless steels in a general PWR environment.

*Importance for LTO beyond 60 years:* The effect on fatigue resistance of RPVIs of radiation hardening, the tendency for localised deformation caused by neutron irradiation, and other radiation consequences should be assessed to anticipate any unexpected damage mechanism.

*Proposals for dispositioning:* Perform fatigue endurance testing of irradiated materials in LWR environments. In case irradiation has a negative impact on the fatigue resistance, develop predictive capability to account for irradiation effects on fatigue resistance, or incorporate irradiation effects in existing fatigue models. Implement the VVER specific research project on the fatigue properties of irradiated Ti-stabilised austenitic stainless steel, with a focus on low-cycle environmental fatigue.

Perform material harvesting of RPV internals in areas sensitive to fatigue.

*Relevant sub-section of the report:* 4.3 Reactor pressure vessel internals

*Conclusion number:* E4.3-06

*Conclusion title:* Swelling and radiation creep of materials of RPVIs

*Description of the conclusion:* The fracture properties of the material and the crystal structure deteriorate in an environment of high neutron fluxes and high temperatures, which are typical for the internals of a high-power reactor with a specific design. An empirical phenomenological model is used to computationally evaluate the evolution of radiation induced swelling and creep. The model is primarily based on data from fast research reactors; too high and too low conservatism can lead to unacceptable results. To ensure the required accuracy of the swelling and creep evaluation, it is necessary to compare the degradation prediction with the actual state of the RPVIs components. This can be done by measuring the creep and swelling induced deformation of selected parts of the RPVIs or by measurement of void swelling development in harvested RPVIs material.

*Importance for LTO beyond 60 years*: Radiation-induced creep and swelling development can influence the fracture properties of the RPVI material and geometry of the RPVI components. Both can lead to the non-ability to full file required functions of the RPVIs. It is necessary to predict degradation development with needed accuracy.

*Proposal for dispositioning:* For nuclear power plants with susceptible materials (currently known for VVERs, potentially also for other PWRs and BWRs), measurement of the RPVI dimensions changes during operation to verify and further develop the model of creep and swell development. Another possibility is the measurement of void swelling development in harvested materials from decommissioned RPVIs. Implement research programmes to investigate fracture properties of irradiated austenitic stainless steel from harvested RPVIs materials for determination or refinement of already established failure criteria.

*Relevant sub-section of the report:* 4.3 Reactor pressure vessel internals

*Conclusion number:* E4.3-07

*Conclusion title:* SCC mitigation by optimisation of water chemistry

*Description of conclusion:* The optimisation of water chemistry to reduce the electrochemical CP has been successfully applied in different RPVs, especially in BWRs, but not exclusively. A reduced electrochemical CP is an effective technique to mitigate SCC and provide a higher level of safety against failures and/or can reduce the inspection efforts. One simple method is the usage of hydrogen water chemistry, but it is more efficient in conjunction with the application of noble metals, like platinum. Also, a combination with zinc has beneficial effects.

*Importance for LTO beyond 60 years:* A consequent optimisation of water chemistry can prevent or delay failures caused by SCC.

*Proposals for dispositioning:* Advanced water chemistry optimisation should be deeply studied to apply them, if relevant, in more nuclear power plants.

*Relevant sub-section of the report:* 4.3 Reactor pressure vessel internals

*Conclusion number:* E4.3-08

*Conclusion title:* Failure criteria for RPVI highly irradiated materials

*Description of the conclusion:* There is a lack in the failure criteria/failure mechanisms for the highly irradiated components of VVER reactors. This issue also might be relevant for the EPR heavy reflector, for which swelling is also relevant.

*Importance for LTO beyond 60 years*: The failure modes and failure criteria for the highly irradiated components, for example the VVER-1 000 baffle and its fasteners, will be different from other RPVIs. Some additional mechanisms, like full embrittlement zones and possible damage analysis with swelling/creep interactions, should be analysed.

*Proposal for dispositioning:* Implement research programmes to address the failure criteria issues for highly irradiated VVER (potentially other PWR or BWR) RPVIs materials from harvested samples.

*Relevant sub-section of the report:* 4.3 Reactor pressure vessel internals

*Conclusion number:* E4.3-09

*Conclusion title:* NDE and ISI methodology for RPVIs

*Description of conclusion:* It is necessary to develop NDE and ISI methods for the RPVI elements, especially those highly loaded and highly irradiated: the baffle (core basket) and its fasteners. It is essential to develop such techniques since they should be applied in aggressive environments where accuracy and time of inspection are important. Also, the development of the ISI methodology may be used to ensure reactor safe operation, prevention of high vibration and wear. The results of ISI may be further used in HCF lifetime prediction.

For the VVER-1 000 internals, the development of geometry measurement techniques is needed to compare with calculated irradiation-induced creep/swelling distortion. Such techniques will be used to adjust the computational model and to have a more reliable prediction of swelling distortion and, as consequence, more reliable predictions of possible baffle/fuel contact.

*Importance for LTO beyond 60 years:* Having such techniques available in the future would be useful for preventing/predicting vibrations and wear, to shorten the maintenance time. For VVERs it is important since baffle measurements are required for every unit during LTO.

*Proposals for dispositioning:* A project focused on the NDE should be implemented and ISI monitoring technics for RPVIs should be considered. Such a project should cover both operational techniques, which can be used when the reactor operates at full power, as well as NDE techniques when the reactor is in maintenance.

*Relevant sub-section of the report:* 4.4 Steam generators

*Conclusion number:* E4.4-01

*Conclusion title:* Cracking of Alloy 800 NG tubing in CANDU SGs

*Description of conclusion:* Based on OPEX of Alloy 800 NG tubing in some European SGs, it is anticipated that Alloy 800 tubing in CANDU SGs is also susceptible to ODSCC, especially at the expansion area near TTS. For risk-informed ISI, there is a need to predict when ODSCC will occur in CANDU SGs. Activation energy for crack initiation and tensile stress due to tube expansion and potential denting due to hard sludge are key inputs for the statistical assessment.

*Importance for LTO beyond 60 years:* Knowing the time when ODSCC occurs will have an important impact in SG ageing management. It will help not only to guide ISI, but also to determine the frequency and method for removing the sludge from the TTS. Widespread ODSCC will likely result in early retirement of SG.

*Proposals for dispositioning:* Monitor the OPEX of Alloying 800 tubing, assess the potential chemistry excursion due to condensate tube leakage, benchmark the statistic and probabilistic assessment method, measure activation energy for crack initiation, and predict and measure denting induced tensile stress.

*Relevant sub-section of the report:* 4.4 Steam generators

*Conclusion number:* E4.4-02

*Conclusion title:* Procedures for repair, replacement, and cleaning of the horizontal SGs VVER 440 MW and 1 000 MW

*Description of conclusion:* Regarding the procedures for repairing the threaded holes of the hot and cold collectors, and the manholes, an appropriate system of controls should be implemented to monitor and evaluate potential ageing effects and their causes. Based on the identified causes of the ageing effects, a suitable repair procedure should be performed.

For the horizontal SGs, due to their size and location within the containment, replacement would be very difficult and expensive. Therefore, it is more appropriate to invest resources in AMP ensuring sufficient NDE, corrective and/or mitigation measures, and research into degradation mechanisms to avoid the need for SG replacement during the nuclear power plant operation. One way to ensure the satisfactory condition of the SG secondary side is through mechanical cleaning using robotic manipulators. Due to possible design deviations between individual SGs, it is necessary to ensure an individualised design of the manipulator for each specific SG.

For all three points discussed, it is necessary to evaluate the condition of the SGs as well as the impacts on the ageing management programme for the SGs of a specific nuclear power plant, to introduce these into the risk register, and then address these risks.

*Importance for LTO beyond 60 years:* Insufficient AMP and lack of cleaning procedures may lead to early damage or decommissioning of the SGs in the future.

*Proposals for dispositioning:* To ensure the LTO of the SGs, it is crucial to implement comprehensive monitoring systems and tailored repair procedures based on identified causes of ageing effects. Invest in preventive measures, such as robotic cleaning and integrat these practices into the AMP.

*Relevant sub-section of the report:* 4.4 Steam generators

*Conclusion number:* E4.4-03

*Conclusion title:* Optimisation of secondary water chemistry

*Description of conclusion:* Secondary water chemistry has a major influence on the volume of deposits developed inside the SG and on the conditions in the SG crevices. In the crevices, there is a high risk of corrosion development. Therefore, secondary water chemistry should be continuously monitored, cleaned through the cleaning stations, and evaluated to maintain its parameters within the stated optimal limits. It is needed to evaluate the impact of secondary water chemistry in the AMP, and it should be addressed and assessed based on the findings.

*Importance for LTO beyond 60 years:* Optimisation of water chemistry, based on continuous monitoring, can prevent or delay failures caused by crevice corrosion under the deposits.

*Proposals for dispositioning:* To prevent failures caused by crevice corrosion under deposits, it is essential to continuously monitor and optimise secondary water chemistry. These measures should be integrated into the AMP.

*Relevant sub-section of the report:* 4.4 Steam generators

*Conclusion number:* E4.4-04

*Conclusion title:* Conservation procedures of the SG secondary side under N2 atmosphere.

*Description of conclusion:* The SG should be preserved under a nitrogen atmosphere during an outage to secure the internal space from oxygen and the development of atmospheric corrosion. Therefore, the work in progress inside and around the SG during the outage should be co-ordinated in a way to keep the SG filled with N2 as long as possible. It is needed to evaluate the impact of contact time of the SG with oxygen in the AMP, and it should be addressed and assessed based on the findings.

*Importance for LTO beyond 60 years:* Preventing access of oxygen to the secondary side of the SG during the outage would prevent the SG from the development of atmospheric corrosion and accelerated ageing.

*Proposals for dispositioning:* The operators of the nuclear power plants should ensure nitrogen preservation of the SG secondary side whenever possible.

*Relevant sub-section of the report:* 4.5 Safety Class 1 piping

*Conclusion number:* E4.5-01

*Conclusion title:* Harmonisation of the numerous approaches for EAF existing in parallel

*Description of conclusion:* Different methods have been developed for appropriately addressing the effects of the LWR environment on the fatigue calculations of nuclear power plants. For instance, in the United States, US NRC regulatory requirements are well developed for addressing EAF during License Renewal activities (for details see APA A4.5-03).

In France, RCC-M code [385] provides explicit rules to address EAF (Rule in Probationary Phase #3). They are based on NUREG/CR-6909 report [188] and are optimised to better account for the effect of influent parameters, following extensive experimental programmes.

#### *Importance for LTO beyond 60 years:*

Although the relationship between the life of a component and the magnitude and frequency of the cyclic loading in LWR environments is well understood, additional testing is recommended to further reduce uncertainties, especially for cases where data are in a more limited number.

*Proposals for dispositioning:* Since different approaches for EAF exist in parallel, more efforts should be made to harmonise the code requirements to better serve as a model for nuclear power plants using different approaches to relicense for LTO.

Additional testing is recommended to further reduce uncertainties in the impact of environment on fatigue calculations of nuclear power plants.

*Relevant sub-section of the report:* 4.5 Safety Class 1 piping

*Conclusion number:* E4.5-02

*Conclusion title:* Current UT examination methods do not exist to reliably apply UT techniques to CASS materials

*Description of conclusion:* The microstructure of CASS materials challenges the reliability of UT examination techniques. As such, the qualification requirements for UT procedures, personnel, and equipment used for examination of CASS piping in accordance with the AMSE BPVC Section XI, Mandatory Appendix VIII have not been developed. The EPRI MRP-479 report [414] describes the PFM approach and results obtained to address the challenges in qualification of UT examinations for CASS piping. PFM analyses assess the structural implication of axial flaws being present in CASS piping and propagating as cracks without crediting in-service examination. Additional PFM analyses assess the structural margin, provided by an alternative flaw evaluation methodology, that does not require depth sizing information upon detection of circumferential cracking.

MRP-479 [414] is intended to support development of Mandatory Appendix VIII, Supplement nine for CASS and alternatives to the current ASME Section XI examination and flaw acceptance requirements for CASS piping components.

*Importance for LTO beyond 60 years:* To disposition the lack of viable inspection methodology, utilities often turn to flaw tolerance evaluations for CASS piping. As the plants age flaw tolerance evaluations become more difficult due to the increasing number of cycles over time.

*Proposals for dispositioning:* Current methods do not exist to reliably apply UT techniques to CASS materials. Therefore, additional analyses to assess the structural margin need to be provided by an alternative flaw evaluation methodology by PFM, when in-service examination cannot be credited upon detection of circumferential cracking.

*Relevant sub-section of the report:* 4.5 Safety Class 1 piping

*Conclusion number:* E4.5-03

*Conclusion title:* Advanced mechanical assessment methods – flaw initiation in CASS

*Description of conclusion:* New methods are identified to reduce the conservative hypotheses of the current analytical approach used in the ductile fracture studies of CASS components. For the assessment of flaw initiation, the development and licensing of a specific criterion considering the lower harmfulness of casting defects, whose morphology does not correspond to planar cracks, would constitute a more realistic approach. Indeed, current ductile fracture studies model defects as planar, which are much more severe than the actual potential casting defects affecting CASS components.

*Importance for LTO beyond 60 years:* The only strong LTO issue for safety Class 1 lines is the thermal ageing of CASS E-elbows (elbows situated on the cold leg close to the RPV). Given that component replacements are not always feasible and that NDE remains a challenge in coarse grains materials, improving the mechanical analysis methodologies is necessary for LTO beyond 60 years. This would allow for a more accurate evaluation of the actual margins available on CASS elbows.

*Proposals for dispositioning:* Make use of laboratory mechanical tests on specimens containing casting defects (shrinkage cavities) to determine a ductile initiation criterion applicable to this type of defects.

*Relevant sub-section of the report:* 4.5 Safety Class 1 piping

*Conclusion number:* E4.5-04

*Conclusion title:* Thermal ageing of Safety Class 1 CASS piping elbows- advanced method to assess crack stability

*Description of conclusion:* New advanced mechanical assessment methods are identified to reduce the conservative hypotheses of the current analytical approach used in the ductile fracture studies of CASS components. For the assessment of ductile tearing resistance, the development and licensing of a criterion based on the Gfr parameter [240] would be beneficial. This parameter is more accurate than the J parameter (Rice integral) currently considered in brittle fracture studies, due to a distinction between plastic and fracture energies.

*Importance for LTO beyond 60 years:* The only remaining LTO issue regarding the thermal ageing of CASS of Safety Class 1 pipelines is the thermal ageing of CASS elbows. Given that component replacements are not always feasible and that NDE remains a challenge in coarse grains materials, improving the mechanical analysis methodologies is necessary for LTO beyond 60 years for these components in order to determine the actual margins available on CASS elbows more accurately. For ductile tearing resistance studies, the licensing of a criterion based on the Gfr parameter would provide a more precise evaluation of the margin than the J parameter currently used today.

It is worth noting that CASS materials properties after ageing are already available to cover up to at least 80 years of service.

*Proposals for dispositioning:* Codification of Gfr criterion in RCC-M code.

*Relevant sub-section of the report:* 4.5 Safety Class 1 piping

*Conclusion number:* E4.5-05

*Conclusion title:* Systems for thermal hydraulic parameters measurement to monitor thermal stratification don't have broad adoption for VVER

*Description of conclusion:* Despite different geometries from unit to unit of VVER-440, the pressuriser surge line is susceptible to significant additional stresses due to the thermal stratification. The available monitoring data from different units confirms a significant temperature gradient along the pressuriser surge line cross-section under certain operational modes. The pressuriser surge line of VVER-1 000 is susceptible to additional stress due to the thermal stratification, although to a lesser extent than in the case of VVER-440. The available monitoring data confirms the temperature gradient along the pressuriser surge line cross-section under certain operational modes. The thermal stratification leads to low cycle fatigue which is especially important for those pipelines that connect the "cold" and "hot" sections of the circuit – pressuriser – MCL. Besides that, it can be especially important during shutdowns of the main circulation pump when conditions for significant thermal stratification may arise due to domination of gravitational forces in the cross section of pipe.

Current monitoring technologies, such as thermocouples distributed around the pipe circumference, are reliable and have been successfully implemented in US plants as part of their licence renewal processes. Plants like [Point Beach](https://eur05.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.nrc.gov%2Fdocs%2FML2032%2FML20329A247.pdf&data=05%7C02%7Cmocanu%40nrg.eu%7Caaf86302f9ac4b46074208dcdbbd143e%7C93c5c58978544f36be51698be705f137%7C0%7C0%7C638626853273555450%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJWIjoiMC4wLjAwMDAiLCJQIjoiV2luMzIiLCJBTiI6Ik1haWwiLCJXVCI6Mn0%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=Qa2%2BNPrVLjpcQEOHqUDYHSipQq5NSkLy6AsC1Pl800U%3D&reserved=0) demonstrate that these techniques can effectively manage thermal stratification over extended operating periods (60- 80 years). But such monitoring systems are not widely implemented for VVER-1 000 and VVER-400 nuclear power plants. Therefore, for calculations to justify LTO, experts have to use data regarding temperature gradient from the literature or similar nuclear power plants where the thermal stratification monitoring is provided.

*Importance for LTO beyond 60 years:* The additional stresses in nuclear power plants piping from thermal stratification must be considered for static strength assessment and low cycle fatigue. During LTO studies in Ukraine, which operates VVER-440 and VVER-1 000, the values of temperature difference from literature or data from similar nuclear power plants are used as one of the requirements of regulatory body. But there is no verified evidence if this value is correct for all nuclear power plants, and how it changes during operation, etc. So, the thermal stratification as the mechanism (event) which lead to degradation such as low cycle fatigue of important sections of nuclear power plants' equipment cannot be accounted for correctly in the analysis.

*Proposals for dispositioning:* Current nuclear power plants' systems for thermal hydraulic parameters measurement are not widely implemented for VVER-440 and VVER-

1 000 nuclear power plants. Therefore, a broader adoption of proven technologies like in US plants to ensure comprehensive monitoring of thermal stratification across all nuclear facilities and enhanced international collaboration needs to be encouraged.

*Relevant sub-section of the report:* 4.5 Safety Class 1 piping

*Conclusion number:* E4.5-06

*Conclusion title:* Development and validation of physical models for accurate predicting leakage from real cracks

*Description of conclusion:* LBB has been adopted in both PWR and CANDU for break exclusion or break preclusion purpose. Leakage calculation is essential and the most uncertain part of either a deterministic or probabilistic LBB assessment. There are limited test data or field observations to validate the cracking opening displacement model and leakage from real service-induced tight cracks.

*Importance for LTO beyond 60 years:* The calculated safety margins could be negatively impacted if leakage prediction models were inaccurate. Additional test data or field measurement will help to reduce uncertainty.

*Proposals for dispositioning:* Broaden participation in international benchmark projects to collectively validate the current leakage prediction software such as LEAPOR [415] and its variant LEAPOR-CANDU [416]; explicitly address the uncertainty in leakage especially for detectable leakage significantly less than 1gpm in the probabilistic assessment using validated codes such as xLPR 2.2 [222] or PRAISE-CANDU 2.1 [232]; and develop a best practice document in selecting leakage prediction models.

*Relevant sub-section of the report:* 4.5 Safety Class 1 piping

*Conclusion number:* E4.5-07

*Conclusion title:* Vibration fatigue by rotating parts or flow-induced

*Description of conclusion:* High cyclic fatigue fractures due to mechanical vibrations are the cause of a frequent number of incidents in nuclear power plants. This phenomenon mainly affects small pipelines of all safety classes but can also occur in Class 1 pipelines. The online fatigue monitoring systems are very well able to detect the fatigue caused by slow temperature changes such as thermal transients and stratification phenomena. They are less capable, or not capable at all, of detecting HCF. Especially susceptible are socket weld seams. Cracks initiating at the weld root are not visible and hard to detect.

The typical causes of vibrations are resonant excitations either caused by rotating parts or flow induced. In the first case, the excitation frequencies are known and can be avoided by design by setting the resonance frequencies outside this range. The causes for flow-induced vibrations are a more complex and manifold. The excitation is of broad banding character, and therefore more difficult to avoid by design. Incidents often occur after power uprates, design modifications or changes of operating procedures. Vibration monitoring systems exist, but the challenge is the large volume of SSC.

*Importance for LTO beyond 60 years:* Vibration-related fatigue is one of the most frequent damage incidents in nuclear power plants. Extending the operating time increases the probability of such failures.

*Proposals for dispositioning:* Develop improved concepts for vibration monitoring that can monitor larger system areas at a reasonable effort.

Develop constructive measures including critical review of support concepts to systematically avoid resonance frequencies in typical excitation ranges. Perform modal analyses systematically for all piping systems, inclusive all the small piping.

Enhance the understanding of fluid-dynamic and hydro-acoustical mechanisms and their interaction with the structure. Further develop appropriate analysis tools.

Avoid the use of socket welds, as these have high notch effect factors at the weld root and cracks that do not penetrate the wall are barely detectable. Medium with poor water chemistry can concentrate in the root gap, which promotes EAC. SDOs and regulators should severely restrict their use, and therefore not accept new piping, system modifications and repairs. Preventive replacement is indicated for areas identified as being vulnerable, but not in general for all socket welds because their number is usually quite high.

*Relevant sub-section of the report:* 4.5 Safety Class 1 piping

*Conclusion number:* E4.5-08

*Conclusion title:* Thermal cycling due to vortex penetration and other complex thermohydraulic phenomena

*Description of conclusion:* While in the past there were some prominent cases of damage caused by turbulent thermal mixing, such as the Civaux event in 1998 on a T-junction of the RHRS, the problem of mixing flows is today largely under control, for example through constructive design with appropriate thermo-sleeves. However, thermal fatigue cracks (in addition to stress corrosion cracks) recently discovered in safety injection lines of some French PWRs call for further investigations to characterise local thermohydraulic phenomena in non-isolable branches.

There are always phenomena that are less well understood, such as the upper plenum injection line issue at Doel in 2018, a similar event recently at a SI line in Krsko or some of the recent French OPEXs with non-isolatable auxiliary piping. All these incidents occurred unexpectedly and involved a complex, resource-consuming and technically challenging root cause analysis.

The detection of fast temperature fluctuations is usually outside the coverage of online fatigue monitoring systems.

*Importance for LTO beyond 60 years:* A better understanding of the phenomena behind the examples mentioned can reduce the number of such cases of failure.

*Proposals for dispositioning:* Enhance the understanding of such complex mechanisms and their interaction with the structure. Further develop appropriate analysis tools.

Develop constructive solutions and mitigation measures to prevent such failures.

Many efforts are already being made to better understand vortex penetration effect, and the transfer of information and operational experiences at the international level is occurring very effectively. This not only provides plants with the knowledge of potential problems occurring in other facilities around the world, but also the possibility to apply the techniques that have proven to be most effective in managing these effects. Additionally, fostering collaboration between plants and experts will be essential to sharing operational experiences and improving the understanding of these complex mechanisms. This approach will lead to better identification of potential risks and more effective preventive actions.

*Relevant sub-section of the report:* 4.5 Safety Class 1 piping

*Conclusion number:* E4.5-09

*Conclusion title:* Application of SCC mitigation methods (e.g. MSIP, FSWOL or other techniques to introduce compressive residual stresses)

*Description of conclusion:* The application of SCC mitigation methods such as MSIP, preventive FSWOL or other techniques to introduce residual compressive stresses in SCC susceptible areas such as DMW provide a higher level of safety against failures and/or can reduce the inspection efforts. Their effectiveness has been demonstrated on various RPVs. However, it seems that the use of such methods is triggered by initiating events or necessities rather than as a proactive approach.

*Importance for LTO beyond 60 years:* The application of these techniques can prevent or delay failures caused by SCC. Compressive stresses also have a beneficial effect on fatigue crack initiation or propagation.

*Proposals for dispositioning:* The application of such methods should be done in more nuclear power plants and in a more proactive manner.

*Relevant sub-section of the report:* 4.6 Buried and underground piping

*Conclusion number:* E4.6-01

*Conclusion title:* The absence of technique for buried and underground piping integrity assessment from permanent ground displacement due to earthquakes

*Description of conclusion:* Permanent ground displacement-induced load due to earthquakes is one of the main calculation issues for integrity assessment of the buried piping. The problem is the absence of a methodology on how to obtain the correct value of permanent ground displacement after seismic influence, depending on its magnitude. The calculation scheme of ground displacements and locations along the piping where displacements should be applied are not defined properly in scientific literature and normative documents too.

*Importance for LTO beyond 60 years:* The seismic analysis is an important part of LTO justification. Permanent ground displacement-induced loads due to earthquakes leads to significant values of stress as a rule and may violate artificially the strength criteria as result. So, the formulation of recommendations on how to obtain the correct input data for the analysis and scheme of soil-pipe interaction for permanent ground displacementinduced load is an important task for LTO justification beyond 60 years for buried and underground piping.

*Proposals for dispositioning:* The technique for buried piping integrity assessment from permanent ground displacement due to earthquakes should be clearly described in the standards. It must include the value of permanent ground displacement after seismic influence depending on its magnitude, the scheme of ground displacements and locations along the piping where displacements should be applied and requirements for mathematical model of piping.

*Relevant sub-section of the report:* 4.6 Buried and underground piping

*Conclusion number:* E4.6-02

*Conclusion title:* Standards for buried pipeline system integrity assessment under seismic

influence

*Description of conclusion:* The standards for buried pipeline system integrity assessment under seismic influence do not include a unified methodology of full dynamic model construction for long and multibranched pipeline systems considering pipeline-soil interaction. They are mostly based on the report "Guideline for the Design of Buried Steel Pipe. ASCE. American Society of Civil Engineers, 2001". The report considers two parts of seismic impact: analysis during the oscillatory process and strength assessment of the from permanent ground displacement (see E4.6-01). However, there are not any unified recommendations for the construction of dynamic models concerning the peculiarities of modeling the pipe-soil interaction, the determination of natural frequencies and modes of vibration, the required length of pipeline section that should be included in the analysis, etc.

*Importance for LTO beyond 60 years:* The seismic analysis is an important part of LTO justification. For buried piping the absence of strict requirements for dynamic model construction and its verification leads to development of numerical model based on scientific research only. So, the results of analysis may differ significantly depending on the engineer qualification, lead to incorrect conclusions and are difficult to review by regulatory body.

*Proposals for dispositioning:* Based on capabilities of specialised software and current scientific research, the methodology for development of a full dynamic model for a long and multibranched buried pipeline system for seismic analysis should be established.

*Relevant sub-section of the report:* 4.6 Buried and underground piping

*Conclusion number:* E4.6-03

*Conclusion title:* NDE methods for selective leaching of buried and underground piping

*Description of conclusion:* Recent research by EPRI (300202030, 3002020830, 302023785) has demonstrated the capabilities of NDE techniques to detect and quantify wall loss that has occurred due to selective leaching in gray cast iron materials. Further testing and demonstration of previously researched techniques would provide additional insights and confidence in the techniques. UT techniques have so far not been effective at detecting and measuring wall loss due to selective leaching when the exam is performed from the same surface as which the degradation is progressing from. Small electromagnetic NDE sensors may offer advantages to detecting wall loss due to selective leaching in more complexly shaped buried cast iron components, such as valve bodies; these have not previously been evaluated.

*Importance for LTO beyond 60 years:* Selective leaching, particularly graphitic corrosion in buried cast iron piping and valves, continues to remain an ageing management challenge due to the difficulties with visual detection of ageing. Added confidence in previously researched NDE techniques, as well as advancements in new techniques, would improve ageing management practices for buried cast iron components.

*Proposals for dispositioning:* Perform additional testing and field demonstrations of NDE techniques on cast iron components. Perform additional research on supplemental techniques not previously evaluated by the referenced technical reports.

*Relevant sub-section of the report:* 4.6 Buried and underground piping

*Conclusion number:* E4.6-04

*Conclusion title:* Cathodic protection effectiveness in complex facilities

*Description of conclusion:* Nuclear power plants generally have large amounts of complex routed buried piping and other assets. Often, these SSCs are commonly connected and electrically grounded for personnel safety reasons. This creates a complex network of SSCs, constructed of different materials, and routed at varying elevations and directions. These factors significantly complicate the assessment of cathodic protection effectiveness on targeted pipes of interest.

*Importance for LTO beyond 60 years:* Cathodic protection is a primary method of mitigating or preventing corrosion on the outside surface of inaccessible buried piping. Understanding the effectiveness of applied cathodic protection in mitigating corrosion of safety-related and other important-to-safety pipelines is important to ensuring the longterm reliability and intended function of such SSCs are maintained throughout plant life.

*Proposals for dispositioning:* Review alternative cathodic protection acceptance criteria as presented in other international standards (e.g. NACE SP0169 [417], ISO 15589-1 [418], EN 14505 [419]). Conduct research to evaluate more effective surveying approaches, adequacy of different acceptance criteria, and modelling capabilities for CP current distribution to optimise CP system design and effectiveness assessments.

*Relevant sub-section of the report:* 4.6 Buried and underground piping

*Conclusion number:* E4.6-05

*Conclusion title:* Non-metallic repair and rehabilitation techniques for buried pipelines

*Description of conclusion:* Due to the costs associated with the excavation and replacement of buried piping, particularly larger diameter pipe, many nuclear power plants are considering and/or already installing non-metallic repair methods (carbon fiber composite, cured-in-place piping, spray-in-place piping). Some of these repair methods are considered only as corrosion barriers or liners, while others are being designed as semi-structural or full-structural in-situ replacements of the existing pipes. Particularly for the semi-structural and full-structural applications, additional research and testing is warranted to:

- non-destructively detect and characterise potential ageing and/or damage;
- understand potential changes in material properties over time;
- develop guidance and standards governing the design, installation, and examination in safety-related piping;
- perform large-scale performance-based testing to validate design assumptions and material properties.

*Importance for LTO beyond 60 years:* Ensure the long-term effects of ageing are properly understood and managed for in-situ repair methods used to replace existing piping systems.

*Proposals for dispositioning:* Conduct additional research and development to:

• develop/evaluate NDE techniques capable of detecting degradation of non-metallic piping materials;

- characterise long-term ageing and strength properties of non-metallic materials (CFRP, SIPP, CIPP);
- develop enhanced guidance and standards governing design, installation, and examination of non-metallic piping materials (CFRP, SIPP, CIPP);
- perform large-scale performance-based testing to validate design assumptions and material properties.

*Relevant sub-section of the report:* 4.7. Concrete containment and civil structures

*Conclusion number:* E4.7-01

*Conclusion title:* Alkali-aggregate reactions and delayed ettringite formation

*Description of conclusion:* The swelling reactions initially compensate for the loss of prestress, which is favourable. Then, it creates a prestress in the reinforcing steels and in the cables, which is no longer favourable. It seems important to know the creep achieved to better understand this risk. Besides, the effect of DEF in the non-prestressed direction is not documented enough and should be studied further. Furthermore, the kinetics of the reaction must be better known, particularly in the presence of reinforcing and prestressing steel. The gels can be swelling without constraint while they are non-swelling with constraint.

*Importance for LTO beyond 60 years:* Concrete swelling pathologies could be a factor limiting for the operating time because no repair solution is currently known.

*Proposals for dispositioning:* Implement appropriate visual inspections with crack counting or crack opening, equip the structures with devices for measuring deformations or stresses when they are adopted, and model the behaviour of the structure. It is also useful to equip prestressed structures to measure creep and better understand the reaction on this type of structure when the swelling operates in a proprietary direction.

As the first impact of AAR and DEF on a structure is local and could affect anchorages before having a global impact on the structure, the consequences of AAR and DEF on the strength of the anchorages of equipment located in the affected zones should be further studied.

*Relevant sub-section of the report:* 4.7. Concrete containment and civil structures

*Conclusion number:* E4.7-02

*Conclusion title:* Modelling of mechanical behaviour of the containment and the steel liner

*Description of conclusion:* The mechanical capacity of the structure to withstand an accident is assessed by ageing calculations based on models that consider the effects of prestressing cable relaxation, concrete shrinkage and creep. The accidental loading is then applied to the model, and the structural analysis is performed by verifying that the calculated stresses and strains are acceptable for civil engineering. To demonstrate the ability of the containment to withstand a severe accident beyond 60 years, improvements to the calculation methods are needed.

*Importance for LTO beyond 60 years:* Concrete containment is a key non-replaceable component. Therefore, having a good modelling of the mechanical behaviour considering all the different degradation mechanisms is essential for LTO beyond 60 years.

*Proposals for dispositioning:* Work on how to evaluate the creep and shrinkage from the erection to date to enable calibration of modelling on the real strains. This is also important for the non-grouted pre-stressing systems because several re-tensioning operations could lead to achieving a level of creep not acceptable for the structure.

*Relevant sub-section of the report:* 4.7. Concrete containment and civil structures

*Conclusion number:* E4.7-03

*Conclusion title:* Fluence impact on concrete biological shield

*Description of conclusion:* The effect of irradiation on concrete is understood but poorly evaluated because the accelerated tests are not perfectly representative and are probably penalising. It is therefore necessary to continue research to reach a consensus on the longterm behaviour of concrete exposed to neutrons and irradiated*.*

*Importance for LTO beyond 60 years:* Prolonged exposure to irradiation may cause a reduction in the mechanical properties and load carrying capacity and therefore may impact the structural integrity of the biological shield.

*Proposals for dispositioning:* Improve the knowledge of concrete exposed to neutrons irradiation by considering the unfavourable effects of the accelerated test of harvested samples exposed beyond the fluence threshold.

*Relevant sub-section of the report:* 4.7. Concrete containment and civil structures

*Conclusion number:* E4.7-04

*Conclusion title:* Non-detection of degradation mechanisms on concrete containment and other civil structures

*Description of conclusion:* Some degradation mechanisms cannot be detected in time to mitigate them. For instance, there might be no available instrumentation for the degradation mechanisms or the instrumentation might be in inaccessible areas. These mechanisms include:

- corrosion activity and changes in the thickness of the coated reinforcement and liner;
- stone nests, delamination, cracking, and concrete defects with an application for swelling pathologies;
- decreases in the concrete stress.

*Importance for LTO beyond 60 years:* A late detection of degradation mechanisms can compromise the ability to mitigate their effects, or repair the safety-related civil structures, compromising the extended service life of nuclear power plants.

*Proposals for dispositioning:* Develop advanced NDE inspection methods enabling the detection and quantification of any degradation mechanisms that could affect concrete containment and other safety-related civil structures*.*

*Relevant sub-section of the report:* 4.7. Concrete containment and civil structures

*Conclusion number:* E4.7-05

*Conclusion title*: Leak tightness of double-wall containments without steel liner

*Description of conclusion:* For double-wall containments without steel liner, loading, stress concentrations, physical and chemical changes of concrete (creep, AAR & DEF, etc.) can lead to small cracks openings in the concrete containment and compromise efforts to meet the leakage criterion (during the ten-year inspection).

*Importance for LTO beyond 60 years:* In the case of LOCA or other severe accidents, it is essential to minimise leaks from the concrete containment building to prevent radionuclide dispersion in the environment.

*Proposals for dispositioning:* The retention of the radionuclides in the concrete wall in case of accident seems to be a margin, even for the single wall containments. It needs to be better quantified. Studies to better quantify radionuclides retention in the concrete wall in case of accident need to be carried out.

*Relevant sub-section of the report:* 4.7. Concrete containment and civil structures

*Conclusion number:* E4.7-06

*Conclusion title:* Assessing effects of coupled degradation mechanisms

*Description of conclusion:* Typically, in codes and standards fundamental degradation mechanisms, their signs and effects are discussed and illustrated for one ageing stressor at a time. However, OPEX shows that various stressors often interact and their effects should therefore be considered. Damage to structural concrete may be attributed to a specific degradation mechanism while it is often simultaneously affected by the benefits or burdens of other degradation mechanisms. These additional important effects could off-set or outweigh the identified root cause.

*Importance for LTO beyond 60 years:* There is a need to examine the effect of relevant coupled degradation mechanisms to understand the visual manifestation as well as fundamental combined mechanisms which can have competing effects. While the effects of some combinations are being studied (e.g. irradiation, elevated temperatures, alkali silica reaction), the effects of other combinations, including those caused by the environmental stressors, are largely unknown.

*Proposals for dispositioning:* Identify and assess the effects of relevant coupled degradation mechanisms.

*Relevant sub-section of the report:* 4.7. Concrete containment and civil structures

*Conclusion number:* E4.7-07

*Conclusion title:* Enhancing protection and repairs using qualified materials applied by the qualified personnel

*Description of conclusion*: Conventional repair techniques and materials are typically used for protection and repair of containment and other safety related structures in nuclear industry. However, it is very important to consider the specifics of nuclear power plants' structures. The importance of using qualified materials applied by qualified personnel cannot be overemphasised.

*Importance for LTO beyond 60 years:* It is necessary to evaluate the performance of applied protections and performed repairs to ensure that protection and repairs result in long-lasting solutions. The following is required:

- incorporating better understanding of ageing in addressing the root cause of degradation;
- incorporating advancements in repair techniques and materials;
- taking advantage of previously performed repairs with good field performance;
- documenting repairs.

*Proposals for dispositioning:* Evaluate the conditions of performed protection and repairs, identify shortcomings in qualified methods, materials and qualifications and address them.

*Relevant sub-section of the report:* 4.7 Concrete containment and civil structures

*Conclusion number:* E4.7-08

*Conclusion title:* NDE methods for steel liner embedded in concrete

*Description of conclusion:* For portions of metallic liner embedded in concrete, there are no available NDE methods that are able to detect degradation of the liner plate. To find different deviations in connection to embedded liner is not possible with the current techniques.

*Importance for LTO beyond 60 years:* Operational experiences show that deviations in the work during construction can cause degradation of embedded pars of the metallic liner. It is not possible to detect the degradation until the liner is penetrated and affects the leak tightness of the containment. With an extended time of operation, there is an increased risk that ongoing degradation reaches the state where the containment's leak tightness is affected.

*Proposals for dispositioning:* Develop NDE methods that can detect either ongoing degradations in the metallic liner or deviations in the constructions.

*Relevant sub-section of the report:* 4.7 Concrete containment and civil structures

*Conclusion number:* E4.7-09

*Conclusion title:* Cleaning method for leak chase system for SFPs

*Description of conclusion:* The steel liner of SFPs is provided with a leak chase system. It is important to ensure that the drainage system channels are free from obstructions, which is stated in section 4.7.4, to be able to detect a leakage through the pool liner. The drainage system is often steel pipes with a small diameter that is embedded in concrete. Often the pipe also has more than one turn of 90 degrees. Clogging of the pipe can be caused by boric crystals or by calcium carbonate from the concrete. The drainage system is hard to inspect and clean because of its design.

*Importance for LTO beyond 60 years:* It is important to ensure that a degradation of SFP liner can be detected if it occurs. If the drainage system is clogged, a leakage would not be detected and the leakage may instead go through the concrete structure.

*Proposals for dispositioning:* Develop methods to inspect and clean the drainage system for the SFP liners.

*Relevant sub-section of the report:* 4.8 Electrical cable systems

*Conclusion number:* E4.8-01

*Conclusion title:* Condition monitoring techniques for low-voltage cables

*Description of conclusion:* Cables are spread throughout the whole plant. Different cable types and insulation materials can complicate the assessment of the actual condition of the cables. A wide range of methods have been proposed. None of them can replace generally accepted destructive EAB measurement. EAB gives clear acceptance end-point-criterion independent of the initial value, which is typically not know for older installations. However, EAB is a destructive technique. Modern non-destructive methods should be developed and put into practice. As mentioned in Section 4.8.3.3, there is currently no single non-destructive testing technique usable on site to assess the ageing of low-voltage cables.

The basic parameter for evaluating the degree of degradation of the cables, or the residual service lifetime, is currently EAB of the insulation. Although electrical measurements may indicate operational problems, the interpretation of the measured results depends on the circumstances of the measurement itself and, above all, on the specific application of the cables in operation. For such electrical measurements, it is very difficult to establish clear acceptance criteria, i.e. service life.

The most important property of any electrical insulation, which determines its intended safety function, is its electrical dielectric strength (insulation resistance). During the cable qualification (IEEE 383), resistance to voltage (electrical strength) is one of the basic tests. It is the only cable property for which the standard directly sets an acceptance criterion. However, commonly performed as well as newly tested methods for evaluating the cable condition do not deal with the correlation with electrical strength. The elevated voltage test is the only way to detect cracks in the insulation of a low-voltage cable operated in a dry environment. Currently, in line with the conclusions of international studies (IAEA TECDOC- 1825 [306], European projects ADVANCE and TEAM Cables, EPRI report 3002020818 [327]), a combination of different characterisation techniques is used to manage the ageing of the low-voltage cables, including visual inspection and some destructive techniques such as EAB measurement.

Recent studies have identified some promising techniques, such as the low-frequency dielectric spectroscopy. However, their effectiveness in monitoring the ageing of installed low-voltage cables remains to be precisely studied, the acceptance criteria for different types of insulation (XLPE, EPR) to be defined, and the deployment in the field, as part of ageing management programmes, to be verified.

*Importance for LTO beyond 60 years:* LTO beyond 60 years concerns the cables manufactured 40-60 years ago. The materials, quality and manufacturing control, with differences between batches, were not as good as now. Testing and qualification procedures performed in the past reflected the current requirements and knowledge. Therefore, it is important to estimate the cable condition instead of relying on the old ageing predictions. Non-destructive CM techniques are very important if samples for EAB are not at disposal.

The absence of on-site NDE techniques for low-voltage cables could lead to premature replacement or failure to detect degradation of low-voltage cables (e.g. in the case of difficult-to-access cables), either along the entire length of the cable or on localised faults (in ALEs).

Moreover, many cables shall operate during DBA. Tests performed before cable installation 40-60 years ago were in many cases accelerated more than would be accepted these days. Verification of the cable condition comparing to the prediction is very important.

*Proposals for dispositioning:* Further investigations and on-site tests are needed. There is a need to assess and develop new and existing non-destructive examination methods and acceptance criteria that can be used during ageing management.

*Relevant sub-section of the report:* 4.8 Electrical cable systems

*Conclusion number:* E4.8-02

*Conclusion title:* Prediction of the evolution of cable characteristics over time

*Description of conclusion:* A predictive approach is essential for LTO of electrical cables beyond 60 years. Characterising the state of ageing of cables at a given point in time through on-site cable sampling or NDE methods is essential but does not allow for optimised cable management over extended LTO. It is necessary to predict when and how cables will deteriorate.

The development of accurate predictive models (such as the "multi-scale" model developed by EDF) is a complex task that requires a thorough understanding of polymer materials, degradation processes and their kinetics. Further research is therefore needed to improve the prediction accuracy of cables degradation over time.

All the models are associated with some uncertainties, which causes, that the predicted lifetime need not be fully justified. Cable CM techniques and cable harvesting procedure shall be used to determine the ageing progress and compare actual cable condition with the prediction. This is a basic method for model verification and continuous models' improvement.

*Importance for LTO beyond 60 years:* Only a predictive approach makes proactive maintenance possible. With a predictive approach, potential problems can be identified and resolved before they cause major failures. This enables proactive rather than reactive maintenance, which can extend the life of cable systems. This also makes it possible to optimise and plan maintenance or replacement operations well in advance.

*Proposals for dispositioning:* The development of predictive models must continue. To confirm their validity, predictive models need to be validated by experimental results, based on the characterisation of cables sampled on site and the results of NDE measurements.

*Relevant sub-section of the report:* 4.8 Electrical Cable Systems

*Conclusion number:* E4.8-03

*Conclusion title:* Determination of 80-year service limiting environment for cable insulation

*Description of conclusion:* As stated in Section 4.8.3.2, the primary goal of a CAMP and of maintaining qualification is to assess and determine the residual lifetime of cables. It is essential to understand the influence of degradation mechanisms on the ageing process, identify which degradation mechanisms affect individual cables at different locations of the nuclear power plant, and establish suitable criteria to estimate the residual lifetime.

For some cable types exposed to harsh conditions, particularly due to high temperatures and radiation in nuclear power plants, sufficient data exist to define service limits for insulation materials over a 40–60 year period, as outlined in EPRI 1013475 [324] (Table 10-1). By identifying nuclear power plants' ALE locations where these harsh conditions exceed stated limits, specific cables can be monitored and managed to mitigate the effects of degradation.

Currently, there is no document or reference that clearly identifies the limiting environment of insulation materials during the period from 60 to 80 years.

*Importance for LTO beyond 60 years:* By implementing these measures, it can be ensured that the AMPs of cables are robust and capable of accurately predicting the lifespan of this type of component, thereby enhancing the safety, reliability and efficiency of nuclear power plants in the extended operational period from 60 to 80 years.

*Proposals for dispositioning:* To address this gap, the development of a comprehensive guideline that outlines how to determine the service limiting conditions for insulation materials when operating from 60 to 80 years is proposed with the aim of getting a similar Table as that defined in EPRI1013475 [324], but applicable for this new period of extended operation. This guideline could include, among others, the following steps/stages:

- 1. Extensive literature review: Thoroughly reviewing existing research and data on the ageing mechanisms and service conditions of various insulation materials, extending beyond the currently documented 40 to 60-year period.
- 2. Accelerated ageing tests: Conducting accelerated ageing tests to simulate the effects of prolonged exposure to harsh conditions (temperature, radiation, moisture, etc.) on insulation materials. These tests should aim to predict the performance and degradation of insulation materials from 60 to 80 years. The most powerful ageing experiments will be by using old cables taken from the plant and pre-age these cables with mild acceleration factors.
- 3. Field data collection: Gathering empirical data from nuclear power plants with long operational histories to identify real-world ageing trends and validate the results of accelerated tests.
- 4. Collaborative research initiatives: Engaging with international bodies such as the IAEA, EPRI and NEA to pool resources and expertise in the development of this kind of guideline.
- 5. Periodic updates: Establishing a process for regularly updating the guidelines as new data and research findings become available.

*Relevant sub-section of the report:* 4.8 Electrical cable systems

*Conclusion number:* E4.8-04

*Conclusion title:* Monitoring of environmental conditions

*Description of conclusion:* The safety guide SSG-69 [12] proposes monitoring of environmental conditions as a very important topic for preserving EQ. Details are provided especially in Sections 5.17 to 5.22 of SSG-69 [12]. The most important parameters to be measured are temperature, dose rate and, in some power plants or for specific equipment, also humidity. All these parameters should be monitored for at least one full campaign, including the period of outage. Not only known hotspots but the whole plant should be monitored. Monitoring should be carried out close to the equipment of scope. Temperature can be measured by self-powered data loggers with the interval of measurement of one hour. Humidity is measured using the same data loggers. Dose rate is typically measured using alanine dosimeters. Alanine in the form of small pellets is placed in respective locations. After one or more campaigns, the dosimeters are removed and evaluated using electron paramagnetic resonance (ESR) spectrometry. Dose rate is calculated from the measured total dose and time of irradiation.

*Importance for LTO beyond 60 years:* Environmental conditions have a significant effect on the rate of ageing of components. For example, a temperature increase of 10°C may accelerate the rate of degradation by a factor of 2–3. Commonly, the design values which were used for initial qualification, are higher than the real measured values. Therefore, these data can be used for re-assessment of qualified life.

Apart from EQ, results from the environmental parameters' monitoring shall be used for the ageing management programme and other areas.

*Proposals for dispositioning:* Implement an environmental monitoring programme. However, such a programme should be spread over the entire plant. Using only a few monitors in hotspots is not sufficient. Information about the environmental parameters' measurement shall be known within the whole plant. Results must be available to all the nuclear power plant personnel, not only to the EQ representative.

*Relevant sub-section of the report:* 4.8 Electrical cable systems

*Conclusion number:* E4.8-05

*Conclusion title:* Importance of the joule (ohmic) heating

*Description of conclusion:* Qualified cables are assumed to be operating at rated full load current and voltage for the duration of the qualified life. However, heating through the passage of electric current, so-called joule heating or ohmic heating, is a significant factor of degradation in power cables. The mechanism of degradation due to this heating is like the effects of heat from the surrounding environment. Prolonged exposure to high temperatures can accelerate the ageing of the cable insulation material. This ageing effect is described in many documents. But only a limited group of power cables continually energising loads (e.g. motors) could be affected by joule heating and a limited amount of equipment important to safety is in continuous operation. This may mean that the real effect is of low importance.

*Importance for LTO beyond 60 years:* A lot of questions arise about the lifetime of cables affected by joule (ohmic) heating. A detailed analysis of the real effect of joule heating on nuclear power plant cables should be carried out.

*Proposals for dispositioning:* An international study should be carried out.

*Relevant sub-section of the report:* 4.8 Electrical cable systems

*Conclusion number:* E4.8-06

*Conclusion title:* Cable lifetime during decommissioning period

*Description of conclusion:* The decommissioning period is commonly not considered in the EQ. Depending on decommissioning strategy, some equipment is needed to be in operation and has a safety function also during this period. Service conditions during the decommissioning period may be different to those during normal operation; e.g. lower temperature but higher humidity. This raises the question of whether decommissioning schedules are defined and whether they can be extended in a similar process as operational plants go to LTO. It also raises the question of whether qualification for DBA ensures sufficient margins.

*Importance for LTO beyond 60 years:* The decommissioning period is commonly not considered.

*Proposals for dispositioning:* An international study should be carried out.

*Relevant sub-section of the report:* 4.9 I&C safety systems

*Conclusion number:* E4.9-01

*Conclusion title:* Obsolescence management of I&C systems

*Description of conclusion:* One of the biggest challenges as I&C systems become obsolete is that the replacements are increasingly digital. These digital replacements perform the same functions but may require additional programmes to be in place (i.e. cybersecurity). They also require additional safety evaluations and common cause failure analyses that would not be required for a like-for-like replacement. Additionally, as digital upgrades to I&C systems are implemented, there needs to be consideration for the digital lifespan being shorter than for the analogue systems. Plans must be in place for the digital lifecycle, including software changes and more frequent hardware upgrades as necessary.

*Importance for LTO beyond 60 years:* Availability of a suitable obsolescence management plan is essential. Without that plan, the operators may not be aware of the obsolescence status of the equipment they have selected as the equipment may have become obsolete by the installation and commissioning phases. It is therefore vital that nuclear power plant operators implement a robust obsolescence management process as soon as practicable, certainly before the nuclear power plant enters the LTO phase of its life cycle.

*Proposals for dispositioning:* A suitable obsolescence management plan for I&C system is necessary so that I&C managers are aware of the obsolete parts in their systems and ensure timely resolution that include procurement plan and system/component replacement on timely manner. This also includes a risk assessment based on the obsolete components' functions and a bridging strategy to ensure system functionality until a permanent solution can be put in place.

*Relevant sub-section of the report:* 4.9 I&C safety systems

*Conclusion number:* E4.9-02

*Conclusion title:* Knowledge management of I&C systems

*Description of conclusion:* Digital upgrades, especially the replacement of safety I&C systems, require access to the original plant design basis, as well as design basis of the original I&C systems. This information for plants older than 40 years may not be available or easily retrievable; however, it is vital for the development of correct and accurate requirements' specification for the new digital I&C systems. Original I&C systems do not always have thorough documentation that describes how the design functions are implemented. There is a potential challenge to upgrading or replacing the original I&C system equipment if personnel knowledgeable about the system is no longer available.

*Importance for LTO beyond 60 years:* In the absence of the original I&C systems' design basis, thorough documentation that describes how the design functions, and knowledge transfer to the I&C personnel, upgrading or replacing the original I&C system equipment may lead to inadequate or even incorrect requirement specifications and, consequently, to incorrect design of safety I&C systems.

*Proposals for dispositioning:* To ensure safety, documentation on the design basis and related information or records relating to I&C systems important to safety need to be controlled through suitable processes, such that they are complete, clear, concise, correct and consistent over the entire life cycle for the I&C system. Implementation of the suitable management system ensuresthat design basis documents and related or derived information or records are sufficient and adequate and are maintained over time to reflect design changes or changing conditions at the plant. This includes documents and information that may be derived from the design basis documentation and that may have an impact on safety, such as procedures or manuals relating to operation, maintenance or modification of such a system (adapted from SSG-39 [420]).

*Conclusion number:* E4.9-03

*Conclusion title:* Licensing uncertainties related to safety digital I&C systems

*Description of conclusion:* Although advanced digital I&C systems have been used extensively in many other industries, their use in the nuclear industry is still very limited. This is mainly because very few new nuclear power plants have been built since the mid-1980s and the licensing process of digital I&C systems is challenging and complex. Digital upgrades are an effective means to enhance plant safety and system functionality, manage obsolescence, and mitigate the increasing failure liability of ageing analogue systems. Unlike analogue technology, there are several technical areas (e.g. reliability determination for digital safety systems, assessment of CCF in safety systems and diverse actuation), where the academic bases or engineering practice supporting the design criteria for I&C safety are not widely accepted by all countries operating nuclear power plants. This may make the licensing of safety digital I&C systems among different vendors across different countries difficult.

*Importance for LTO beyond 60 years:* Digital upgrades of safety I&C systems require clear regulatory requirements, good nuclear standards, as well as co-ordinated efforts among vendors, operating organisations and the regulatory body. Recent experience with newbuilt nuclear power plants in Europe shows that the licensing-related uncertainties may lead to delays in the construction and commissioning of newly built nuclear power plants.

*Proposals for dispositioning:* Co-ordinated efforts among countries operating nuclear power plants is necessary to harmonise licensing practices on digital I&C, especially in several technical areas where the practices differ. There is a co-ordinated effort led by standard development organisations, such as IEC and IEEE, that develops dual logo standards between IEC and IEEE. This could be a way to obtain a good technical basis to achieve a consensus (e.g. among regulators).

*Relevant sub-section of the report:* 5.1 Availability of original design basis documentation

*Conclusion number:* E5.1-01

*Conclusion title:* Management of DBD

*Description of conclusion:* As discussed in Section 5.1, the availability of up-to-date DBD is a precondition for safe LTO, both for modification/configuration management and identification of TLAAs. The results of the IAEA SALTO peer review service, which are analysed in SALTO Highlights 2005-2015 [408], SALTO Highlights 2015-2018 [409] and SALTO Highlights 2018-2022 [39], mention that "DBD is frequently not adequately managed to ensure its availability for the plant".

From this perspective, many nuclear power plants decided to retrieve or reconstitute DBD, which is a complex, expensive and long-term task.
